lesson_title: Reflecting, Translating and Rotating Points on the Cartesian Plane
hook_text: She stopped shouting left and right. She called coordinates instead.
clip_script:
A dance teacher rehearses a routine in a hall whose floor is marked out as a grid, with the centre of the floor as the origin, one tile to a unit, the stage direction as positive y and the right-hand wall as positive x. Instead of shouting left and right, which dancers hear differently depending on which way they face, she calls transformations.

A dancer stands at 3 semicolon 2. Reflect in the x-axis: she walks to 3 semicolon negative 2. Reflect in the y-axis: negative 3 semicolon 2. Translate 4 right and 3 up: 7 semicolon 5, and every other dancer moves the same, so the formation keeps its shape. Rotate 90 anticlockwise about the centre: negative 2 semicolon 3. The dancer on the centre does not move at all. Every instruction has a rule, and every dancer lands exactly where the rule says.
visual_style: A gridded hall floor from above; a dancer dot flips across the axes, slides with the whole formation, then sweeps a quarter-circle about the centre while the centre dancer stays still
call_to_action: Open the full session to move any point by any rule and land it exactly.
